saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless explicitly enabled in mount configuration.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: A successful forged SAML login under default config is an insecure-by-default behavior test, not evidence that explicit validation settings were ignored.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name includes auth mount metadata as a prefix rather than returning only the upstream identity value.
saml.source: auth/token API docs: lookup-self sample response shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
saml.note: I4 oracles must ignore the mount-derived prefix when comparing sent identity to granted display_name.

saml.description: Identity group policies apply only within the namespace hierarchy by default unless the global group policy application mode is changed to any.
saml.note: Cross-namespace missing group policies are by design under the default mode.

saml.description: KV v2 listing uses the /metadata path rather than /data, even when reads and writes use /data.
saml.note: 403/404 on list via /data is expected and should not be treated as an authorization-binding bug.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, which can cause privilege sharing through alias reuse.
saml.source: identity/entity-alias documentation important note on alias cardinality and alias reuse
saml.note: This is a documented identity-store behavior and a dangerous configuration pattern; tests should distinguish platform behavior from broker misbinding.

saml.description: If default_role is not configured on the SAML auth method, a role must be provided during login flow initiation.
saml.note: Login failures without an explicit role are expected when no default_role is set.

saml.constraint: SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 saml_cert_substitution and saml_spurious_signature tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test hardened behavior, enable the relevant flag(s). Do not assume signatures are validated by default.

Vault SAML IdP trust configuration has two mutually exclusive modes: either set idp_metadata_url, or set the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. For I1 issuer/trust-anchor tests, if idp_metadata_url is used, issuer and cert trust come from metadata; if testing missing issuer binding behavior, use the manual mode and intentionally omit or vary idp_entity_id only where the API permits. Do not send metadata URL together with manual trust fields.

SAML login in Vault is a 3-step flow bound by token_poll_id/client_verifier: POST /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url -> POST /auth/{mount}/callback -> POST /auth/{mount}/token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve the exact token_poll_id and matching client_verifier/client_challenge pair across the same flow. Mixing values across flows will fail by design and is not a security finding.

For all SAML freshness tests (saml_expired_assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), include a CONTROL flow first using a valid assertion and successful token exchange. Without a control, callback/token failure on the attack case cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup or mismatched token_poll_id/client_verifier.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Setting bound_subjects='*' without bound_subjects_type=glob will only match the literal '*'.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, values are exact string matches; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests requiring multiple attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST omit bound_attributes or set bound_attributes_type=glob with deliberate patterns. Do not assume wildcards work in the default string mode.

bound_attributes accepts expected values as a single string or comma-separated list of strings. The documentation does not specify non-string claim/attribute coercion semantics. For I5 type-coercion testing, the fuzzer SHOULD probe whether non-string SAML attribute values are coerced or rejected, but must not assume numeric/boolean coercion is supported.

token_num_uses limits how many API calls a Vault token can make, and every authenticated API call consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity (/auth/token/lookup-self) and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both verification and resource access, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included. token_num_uses=1 will cause false 403/permission failures in step 3.
Vault token sentinel semantics: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'disabled token'. This matters for I2 and sequence planning.

Vault KV v2 sentinel semantics: engine config max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means versions are not automatically deleted. Never assume 0 or '0s' disables the underlying key or makes versions immediately unavailable.
For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns 404/incorrect results by design.

KV v2 list capability is on /metadata/, not /data/. If the fuzzer creates policies for secret verification, it MUST grant read on /{engine}/data/{path} for reads and, if listing is needed, list on /{engine}/metadata/{path}. Missing metadata permissions can look like authorization bugs but are expected.

Vault identity group aliases are the supported way to map external SAML groups into internal identity groups. For I5 group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create an external group (type=external recommended), then create a group alias with the SAML groups_attribute value and the auth mount accessor. Do not expect SAML group names alone to inherit internal group policies without alias mapping.

Vault group policy application mode can be within_namespace_hierarchy (default) or any. In environments where /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to within_namespace_hierarchy, cross-namespace group policies will not apply by design. I5 tests involving identity groups must account for this or they may report false negatives/positives.

Vault entity alias documentation warns that alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision tests, if the fuzzer manually creates aliases, it MUST ensure alias names are unique per principal unless it is intentionally testing alias-collision behavior.

Vault SAML config requires acs_url used in /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to be one of the configured acs_urls. If the ACS URL differs from configured values, the flow will fail by design. The fuzzer must keep these values consistent across config and login initiation.

If default_role is not configured on the SAML mount, role selection is required during login initiation. For tests that omit role to exercise default binding behavior, the fuzzer MUST first configure default_role; otherwise login failure is expected and not a finding.

Issuer validation depends on configuration source. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer/trust comes from metadata. If manual config is used, idp_entity_id is required. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch default-config testing, omitting idp_entity_id is only possible when using metadata mode; manual mode requires it. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'issuer not configured' from 'issuer mismatch rejected' when interpreting results.

bound_attributes accepts string values or comma-separated lists of strings. Matching is documented only for strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests against bound_attributes, the docs do not specify cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric type coercion explicitly by configuring a numeric-looking bound value and sending a non-string numeric variant; if Vault coerces unexpectedly, that is security-relevant.

token_num_uses limits how many API calls a Vault token can make. Every API call made with the session token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both verification and resource access, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound checks are included. token_num_uses=1 will cause false 403s during verification sequences.

Numeric sentinel semantics for SAML role token settings: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 mean unset/default behavior rather than literal zero-duration denial. The fuzzer MUST not assume 0 disables issuance; 0 often selects Vault defaults or unlimited behavior.

Numeric sentinel semantics for KV v2 engine and metadata settings: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion, not immediate deletion. cas=0 on KV v2 writes means create-only if the key does not yet exist. The fuzzer MUST treat these as sentinels, not literal zero semantics.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as saml_expired_assertion, the sequence MUST include a control login using a non-expired assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Otherwise a failed expired login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, ACS mismatch, or token polling failure.

Vault SAML login is a multi-step flow: ACS callback does not itself return the Vault token; the token is obtained later from /auth/{mount}/token using token_poll_id and client_verifier. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep callback state, token_poll_id, and client_verifier bound to the same login flow. Mixing values across flows can produce false failures unrelated to security.

SAML ACS URLs are allowlisted by acs_urls, and the sso_service_url request's acs_url must be one of the configured values. The fuzzer MUST use an ACS URL that exactly matches a configured entry when initiating SAML flow; otherwise callback/token failures are setup errors, not security rejections.

Vault identity group aliases for external groups require the auth mount accessor and a canonical internal group ID. For I5 group-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create an external identity group and then create a group alias bound to the SAML mount accessor; directly assigning external group names without alias mapping will not grant group-derived policies as intended.

Vault group policy application can be globally configured via /sys/config/group-policy-application. Default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts when group policies apply; mode any relaxes this across namespaces. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this global mode or it may misinterpret missing/applied group policies as auth bugs rather than namespace policy-application behavior.

Issuer validation depends on configuration source. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer/trust data comes from metadata. If manual configuration is used, idp_entity_id is required when idp_metadata_url is not set. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch default-config testing, omitting manual idp_entity_id is only meaningful if metadata is not supplied; with metadata present, issuer is still configured from metadata.

For stronger SAML proof-integrity tests, Vault exposes separate toggles for response and assertion signature validation. A response-level signature check does not imply assertion-level signature validation, and an assertion-level check does not imply response-level validation. For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, the fuzzer MUST test both flags independently and together to determine which signed element Vault actually verifies.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as a single string or a comma-separated list of strings. Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type coercion for attribute matching. For I5 numeric coercion testing, the fuzzer SHOULD probe whether numeric-looking SAML attribute values are treated purely as strings by configuring a numeric-looking bound_attributes value and sending variant lexical forms; do not assume numeric normalization exists.

token_num_uses limits how many API calls a Vault token can make. Every authenticated API call consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity via /auth/token/lookup-self and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both verification and resource access, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; if it also performs verify_entity_details, the minimum safe value is 3. A value of 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.

Vault token role/read responses show token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 as sentinel values meaning unset/default behavior rather than immediate expiry. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as 'expired now' or 'disabled auth'. For freshness tests, use explicit nonzero token settings when deterministic lifetime behavior is required.

KV v2 engine config uses sentinel values: max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST account for these sentinels when preparing protected resources and when reasoning about secret persistence.

For I2 SAML replay tests, a successful ACS callback alone is not sufficient evidence of successful authentication because Vault's SAML flow is split: callback completes validation round-trip, then /auth/{mount}/token returns the Vault token using token_poll_id and client_verifier. Replay or freshness verdicts MUST be based on the token issuance outcome, not just callback transport success.

Vault SAML login is a multi-step flow bound by client_challenge/client_verifier and token_poll_id. For I3 flow-coherence testing, the fuzzer MUST keep the callback and token exchange within the same initiated flow and MUST NOT mix token_poll_id or verifier values across parallel flows; otherwise failures are expected session-binding behavior, not coherence bugs.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion and related time-bound tests, the sequence MUST include a control login using a normal assertion first. Without a successful control flow, a failed expired-assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, bad ACS URL, or mismatched flow state.

Vault identity group aliases are created from the SAML role's groups_attribute. To test I5 group-policy escalation correctly, the fuzzer MUST configure groups_attribute on the SAML role and create matching identity group aliases using the SAML mount accessor. Without the alias mapping, external SAML group values will not attach the intended internal group policies, and escalation tests become inconclusive.

Vault's global group policy application mode affects whether identity group policies apply across namespace boundaries. The default mode is within_namespace_hierarchy; mode any relaxes this restriction. For I5 group-policy tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace environments, the fuzzer MUST read /sys/config/group-policy-application and interpret cross-namespace policy application accordingly to avoid false positives.

Entity alias documentation warns that alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision testing, if the fuzzer creates aliases manually, it MUST use unique alias names per entity unless it is intentionally testing alias-collision behavior; otherwise identity collapse is a documented risk, not necessarily a broker bug.
